records.authors: Werner Güth; Rolf Schmittberger; Bernd Schwarze
records.title: An experimental analysis of ultimatum bargaining
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Original two-stage game, responder may reject proposer allocation with both losing payoff; experimental foundation for credible rejection.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Positive offers in this game can be strategic to avoid rejection; no unilateral power without retaliation tested.

records.authors: Anthony Ziegelmeyer; Katrin Schmelz; Matteo Ploner
records.title: Hidden costs of control: four repetitions and an extension
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Four repetitions N=476: control-induced motivational crowding mostly confirmed, but economic incentive gains often larger. Separate N=228 flat-fee extension found stronger control costs under hypothetical incentives.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Replicates Falk/Kosfeld 2006 C01-C12 prior corpus, yet DOES NOT replicate the strong general claim that abandoning control always maximizes principal payoffs. Portal's 2025 migration timestamp is NOT actual publication year (2012).

records.title: Preferences for power
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Power Game experiments: more than one quarter participants pay own money to control another's payoffs even with no direct monetary benefits; valuation increases with direct control and discretionary scope.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Power-seeking for its own sake is measurable and adverse to blanket benevolent-power story, BUT power preference != intention to erase B or demonstrated abuse; contrast Ferreira/Hanaki/Tarroux 2020 self-reliance finding in different design.

records.title: Decision Rights: Freedom, Power, and Interference
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Original dynamic psychological game and incentivized laboratory measures distinguish independent freedom, power, interference; aversion to others' interference best explains rights-valuing in this study.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: 2014 SSRN posting revised 2017 = one working paper, peer-reviewed final outlet unverified. Ferreira/Hanaki/Tarroux 2020 found self-reliance instead, methodological non-identical: conflicting constructs are no independent exact replication.

records.authors: Misato Inaba; Yumi Inoue; Satoshi Akutsu; Nobuyuki Takahashi; Toshio Yamagishi
records.title: Preference and strategy in proposer’s prosocial giving in the ultimatum game
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: N=121 participant original four-game within-subject experiment: making proposer's intentionality ambiguous to recipient increased unfair offers; results not mediated by expectation of higher acceptance, consistent with preference-based image/intention concerns.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Observed prosocial offer decline is not proof ultimate welfare preference disappeared; choice/game description and perceived responsibility influence. No B autonomy, identity persistence or genuine no-evaluation setting.

records.title: The entitlement effect in the ultimatum game – does it even exist?
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Original 3 new experiments 1254 total subjects, two laboratory one online: failed to reproduce entitlement effect (earned proposer authority causing smaller offers) across tests and pooled data.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Role-selection impact is not robust; cannot infer universal 'earned power inevitably exploits'. Earliest online 2018 vs issue 2020 same single paper/data. Null effect is not proof a zero effect in every context.

records.title: Implicit communication in the ultimatum game
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Modified ultimatum games show responder costly rejection partly signals disapproval; proposer offers more if can infer response; independent second design with forwarded RANDOM offer alters responder rejection to avoid appearing envious.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: Observed veto is partly social signaling, not purely own fairness or welfare objective. Random offers reduce direct proposer responsibility but also change receiver interpretation; no B independent existence.

records.title: Team building and hidden costs of control
records.empirical_or_formal_scope: Team-building group history raised later agents' effort, but stronger control after shared coordination induced larger effort reductions than in separate-work baseline; combining two individually helpful practices induced unintended crowding out.
records.critical_limit_or_counterevidence: A relationship history can change perceived legitimacy of A control. It does not imply B always prefers a hierarchy or A benefits under no future dependence; publisher journal year 2016 vs 2012 working version one study.
